title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Objects for National Consciousness
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: What do we call official physical or abstract objects that represent the unique identity, sovereignty, and shared unity of a sovereign country?
options: National Disasters
National Corporations
National Symbols
Electoral Manifestos
questions.explain: **National Symbols** are officially recognized objects (like the flag, coat of arms, or anthem) that project the unique identity, history, and sovereignty of a nation, fostering patriotism.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In the Nigerian **Coat of Arms**, what does the large *Black Shield* explicitly represent?
options: The dark history of British colonial rule
The fertile, good soil of Nigeria capable of extensive agriculture
The petroleum wealth hidden in the Niger Delta
The vast military strength of the armed forces
questions.explain: In the Nigerian Coat of Arms, the **Black Shield** symbolizes the **good and fertile soil** of the nation, while the silver 'Y' bands on it represent the Niger and Benue rivers.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The Nigerian National Flag, a vital national symbol, consists of green and white stripes. What does the green color specifically stand for?
options: Peace and Unity
Agricultural wealth and abundant natural resources
Blood shed by early patriots during the civil war
The dominance of a single political party
questions.explain: The green stripes on the Nigerian national flag stand for the nation's **agricultural wealth and natural endowments**, whereas the white stripe in the middle represents peace and unity.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following serves as the official **National Currency** that represents Nigeria's economic sovereignty in everyday transactions?
options: The United States Dollar
The British Pound Sterling
The CFA Franc
The Naira and Kobo
questions.explain: The **Naira and Kobo** were introduced in 1973 as the official legal tender (National Currency) of Nigeria, replacing the Nigerian Pound.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) is a prominent National Institution. What was the primary constitutional purpose behind its establishment in 1973?
options: To secretly train civilian youths for frontline combat missions
To promote national unity, reconciliation, and integration among youths from diverse ethnic backgrounds
To permanently extract manual labor from youths without compensation
To force Nigerian youths to relocate to foreign countries as expatriates
questions.explain: Following the Nigerian Civil War, the **NYSC** was established to rebuild the nation and **promote national unity** by deploying young graduates to serve in states other than their state of origin, fostering cultural integration.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: To further drive national consciousness, the Federal Government established **Unity Schools** (Federal Government Colleges) across the country. What is the core aim of these schools?
options: To cater exclusively for the children of politicians
To segregate students completely based on their ethnic languages
To bring secondary school students from varying geographic and ethnic zones together, breaking down ethnic prejudices
To prepare students solely for foreign universities
questions.explain: The **Unity Schools** were specifically created as a social experiment to foster early interaction among young students from vastly different ethnic and cultural backgrounds, actively working to break down prejudices and promote unity.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following social practices acts as a potent, everyday way of promoting genuine **National Unity** among Nigerian citizens?
options: Practicing intense ethnic discrimination at the workplace
Fostering inter-marriage across different tribes and cultural backgrounds
Consistently spreading fake political manifestos
Voting exclusively based on religious affiliations
questions.explain: **Inter-marriage** (marrying someone from a different tribe or region) physically and socially unites families across ethnic divides, powerfully breaking down prejudices and promoting national unity.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: While the National Anthem is a song of patriotism, the **National Pledge** acts as an official declaration of what?
options: The military superiority of the Nigerian Armed Forces
An individual's solemn vow of loyalty, commitment, and dedication to the Nigerian State
A guarantee of free tertiary education for every citizen
The supremacy of traditional rulers over democratic institutions
questions.explain: The **National Pledge** is a solemn oath and a direct promise made by citizens expressing absolute loyalty, dedication, and patriotic commitment to defend and uphold the honor of Nigeria.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: To prevent the dominance of one or a few ethnic groups in the governance and public service of the nation, the Nigerian government established a principle called:
options: The Federal Character Principle
The Indigenization Decree
The Unitary Control System
The Universal Suffrage Act
questions.explain: The **Federal Character Principle** was enshrined in the constitution to ensure equitable distribution of wealth, public service positions, and socio-economic privileges across the varying ethnic and regional divides, thereby avoiding marginalization.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following values is defined as the ability to accept, respect, and peacefully coexist with people whose opinions, ethnic backgrounds, or religious beliefs are entirely different from yours?
options: Intimidation
Discipline
Tolerance
Contentment
questions.explain: **Tolerance** is a massive pillar of national unity. It requires citizens to peacefully accept and respect the cultural, political, and religious diversity that exists within a heterogeneous country like Nigeria.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A key way of promoting national unity is through **Hospitality**. In a civic context, what does hospitality entail?
options: Forcing foreigners to pay extra taxes for basic goods
Creating a friendly, generous, and welcoming environment for strangers and fellow citizens from different regions
Refusing to do business with individuals outside your state of origin
Admitting only indigenes into local community hospitals
questions.explain: **Hospitality** is the warm and generous reception of guests, visitors, or strangers. When practiced across regional lines, it breaks down fear and stereotypes, effectively promoting national unity.

questions.q:
Evaluate the table below showing actions and their impact on National Unity:

| Action | Impact on National Unity |
|---|---|
| Inter-marriage | Positive |
| Tolerance | Positive |
| $Z$ | Negative |

Which of the following correctly replaces $Z$?
options: Non-discrimination
Participation in NYSC
Ethnic nepotism and bigotry
Displaying the National Flag
questions.explain: Actions like **ethnic nepotism and bigotry** breed hatred, suspicion, and division, negatively impacting National Unity. The other options promote integration.

questions.q: The Nigerian Coat of Arms is a prominent symbol of national consciousness. It features two striking white horses on either side of the shield. What do these two white horses officially represent?
options: The military strength of the Nigerian Army
The rich agricultural soil found in the savanna
The dignity and pride of the Nigerian nation
The vast petroleum resources in the South
questions.explain: In the Nigerian Coat of Arms, the **two white horses** flanking the shield officially symbolize the **Dignity and Pride** of the nation.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In the Nigerian National Anthem, the powerful phrase *"The labor of our heroes past, shall never be in vain"* is primarily intended to evoke which of the following sentiments among citizens?
options: A desire to forcefully colonize neighboring West African states
Deep patriotism, urging citizens to work hard to uphold the legacy and sacrifices of the founding fathers
A strict requirement to permanently memorize historical dates
The encouragement of intense regional tribalism and conflict
questions.explain: This specific line in the anthem promotes **National Consciousness and Patriotism**, inspiring the current generation to honor the struggles of past heroes by contributing positively to the nation's continuous growth.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: To ensure equal representation, Nigeria utilizes the **Federal Character Principle**. What is the central aim of this institutional principle?
options: To ensure that all states produce exactly the same amount of agricultural crops annually
To enforce a uniform cultural language across all federal ministries
To ensure there is no unfair predominance of persons from a few specific states or ethnic groups in the government and its agencies
To systematically strip local governments of their constitutional funding
questions.explain: The **Federal Character Principle** mandates that public appointments and amenities reflect the linguistic, ethnic, and geographic diversity of the country, actively preventing the marginalization or dominance of any one group.
